    • getAction

      public GuardAction getAction()
      What the caller should do with the text.

    • getFindings

      public List<GuardFinding> getFindings()
      Every detection, never null.

    • getReasons

      public List<String> getReasons()
      Low-precision detections that were recorded but did not influence the action.

      Surfaced so an operator can see what the guard noticed without it becoming a block.

    • getRedacted

      public String getRedacted()
      The rewritten text. Non-empty only when the action is GuardAction.REDACT.

    • getRiskScore

      public int getRiskScore()
      0..100. min(100, sum(severity_weight * confidence)).

    • getRiskSeverity

      public String getRiskSeverity()
      The band of getRiskScore(): low, medium, high or critical.

    • getPolicySource

      public String getPolicySource()
      project when an operator's stored AIDR policy was applied, default when the product default was.

      Only project is binding: a monitor-mode call cannot lift a block that an operator's own policy mandates.

    • isPolicyEnforced

      public boolean isPolicyEnforced()
      Whether the applied block is mandated by the operator's policy rather than by rule precision alone.

      Lets a caller receiving an unexpected block tell a detection change from a policy change.

    • failedOpen

      public boolean failedOpen()
      Whether the guard was unreachable and the configured fail mode decided the outcome.

      Never silently true: a warning is logged whenever it is set.

    • isBlocked

      public boolean isBlocked()
      Convenience for getAction() == GuardAction.BLOCK.

    • safeText

      public String safeText(String original)
      Returns the text that is safe to send: the redaction when there was one, the original otherwise.

      Exists so no caller has to write the equivalent conditional, which is easy to get wrong in the direction that forwards the secret. Also returns the original when a malformed redact verdict carries no text, rather than silently substituting an empty prompt.
